speaker_role: current admissions officer (Johns Hopkins University admissions counselor)
key_insights: Explains Johns Hopkins' holistic review considers every part of an application in context, so no single factor (e.g. GPA) dominates the outcome.
Describes three evaluation 'lenses' used: academic character, impact/initiative, and overall university match.
Academic character is assessed mainly via letters of recommendation and curriculum rigor, showing academic interest and performance in and out of class.
Impact/initiative looks at engagement outside class time, including non-traditional activities like caregiving for family, part-time work, or cultural/religious involvement.

Match considers whether the applicant's academic and extracurricular profile, essays, and recommendations suggest they'll take advantage of Hopkins' specific opportunities (academic flexibility, hands-on/collaborative environment).
States the personal essay and Hopkins-specific supplemental essay are used to show how an applicant would engage with the university's specific offerings.
notable_or_distinctive: Provides Johns Hopkins' specific named framework of three review 'lenses' (academic character, impacted initiative, match) rather than generic holistic-review language.
reliability_notes: Official promotional admissions-office video; framework is Hopkins-specific and may not generalize to other schools' holistic review processes.
